latest.text:
Tiafoe beat Cobolli 7–6, 6–0 in his second group match in Turin to win his first match at this event. It was the first appearance here for both players and Cobolli played it at home.

The first set was a real fight. Cobolli broke in the opening game and Tiafoe only got level at 3–3. Tiafoe then had a set point on Cobolli's serve but Cobolli saved it and forced a tiebreak. Tiafoe took that tiebreak 8–6. For him, the break back was the moment the set changed: "Just fighting. Like, you know, I felt like after I got the break back, I was a better player in the set." After the tiebreak, Cobolli did not win another game. Tiafoe broke three times and took the second set 6–0.

That second set was built on his return. He won 35% of the points against the first serve, far above his usual 26%.

Credit to him: in his first appearance at this event, he beat the home player on a fast indoor court, with a dominance ratio of 1.64. Medvedev waits in his last group match.

latest.text:
Alcaraz beat Medvedev for the 8th time in 11 meetings, 6–2, 6–4 in the group stage. Alcaraz won 7 games in a row from 1–2 down in the first set. Alcaraz landed 56% of his first serves, compared with his 68% average on hard over the last 52 weeks, and won 74% of his first-serve points (20 of 27) and 76% of his second-serve points (16 of 21), compared with his usual 56%. His first-serve percentage is something to watch in the next round. Returning, Alcaraz won 24% of the points against the first serve (7 of 29), compared with his usual 34%. Alcaraz faced no break points. Medvedev struggled on his second serve, winning 39% of the points (7 of 18), compared with his 49% average on hard over the last 52 weeks. Alcaraz returned very well, with an 8.9 return quality. Medvedev ended with a 9.0 serve quality and 33% unreturned serves. Alcaraz was clearly the better player from the baseline (31–16).

Alcaraz won the first set 6-2 in 31 minutes in a very one-sided start and he went for his shots from the beginning. His returns did much of the damage, including a strong return off a big second serve from Medvedev and he kept breaking serve while covering the whole court. Medvedev looked lost, shrugging his shoulders and shaking his head as the breaks went against him. Alcaraz briefly lost focus and gave up break chances but he held on. Alcaraz preferred the faster court in Turin to the slower court at Indian Wells, where Medvedev had beaten him. He finished with a one-sided win, looked relaxed throughout and moved to two wins from two matches this week.

Physically, it is something to follow. Alcaraz took a medical timeout at 2–1 in the second set. We do not know the reason. Something to follow up for the next round.
